sources.title: Spectroscopic and XRD data from PHS

protocol.freeze_scope: Protocol, sample correspondence, transforms and descriptive outcomes frozen after native-header and primary-method inspection, before calculating field/lab comparison outcomes. This is a known, previously published control, not a blind discovery experiment.
protocol.question: How consistent are the archived same-specimen field and laboratory VNIR reflectance spectra on declared common analysis support, compared with different-specimen pairings from the same archive?

study.title: Spectroscopic Studies on the Puga Hot Spring Deposits, Ladakh, an Astrobiological Martian Analog Site in India
study.source_access: Primary full text inspected through web retrieval on 2026-11-14. Later section requests timed out; no unavailable table was transcribed.
study.vnir_unit_evidence: Section 4.1 identifies spectral reflectance measured with FieldSpec 4 Hi-Res over 350-2500 nm, standardized with Spectralon, using a lamp/contact probe in the field. The instrument has stated resolution 3 nm at 700 nm and 8 nm at 1400/2100 nm; complete response functions are not provided.
study.ftir_unit_evidence: Section 4.2 gives 4000-400 cm^-1, 4 cm^-1 resolution and transmittance-mode KBr pellets. Native CSV files do not label the ordinate scale; do not interpret their amplitudes as physical transmittance or absorbance.
study.prior_art: The study already establishes Puga as a Martian analogue. These files do not support a new-site discovery claim.

xrd.evidence: Native RAW4 headers and [Data] column labels; no physical ordinate conversion or phase assignment

protocol.sample_identity_policy: Only the following explicit filename-to-specimen map establishes correspondence. Zero padding and export punctuation are normalized here, not by fuzzy matching. Names are archive specimen IDs, not independently verified chain-of-custody records or mineral labels.

transform.native_wavelength_conversion: wavelength_um = wavelength_nm / 1000; never reinterpret FTIR wavenumbers as VNIR wavelengths
transform.bin_method: Exact trapezoidal integral of the native piecewise-linear reflectance divided by bin width; retain a bin only with full positive finite native support and no gap above max_native_gap_um. No extrapolation or interpolation across invalid samples.
transform.response_claim: Declared common 20 nm box-average analysis support, not an exact measured instrument spectral-response match and not an EMIT or CRISM simulation.
transform.invalid_policy: Preserve native values; nonpositive or nonfinite VNIR values invalidate intersecting bins. Values above 1 are retained without clipping. No source quality mask is supplied, so positive finite values are numerically usable, not independently quality-certified.
transform.mask_policy: No outcome-selected band exclusions or detector-splice correction. No atmospheric correction is invented for contact-probe spectra.

protocol.continuum_method: For each window, form a line through the mean wavelength and mean reflectance of all valid bins in each shoulder. Require every requested shoulder and search bin to be valid. Divide search reflectance by this positive continuum. Report 1 minus its minimum, that bin center, and whether the minimum touches a search edge. Preserve negative apparent depths. These broad diagnostics do not identify minerals.

outcomes.matching: All same-ID field/lab pairs in the explicit map. Compare each of those field spectra with every lab spectrum in this paired set, keeping all different-ID comparisons as within-archive specimen mismatch controls. These are not certified different-mineral negatives.
outcomes.summary: Descriptive matched versus mismatch medians and ranges, each field's same-ID rank with ties retained for both SAM and continuum RMSE. No threshold tuning, p-values, independent-sample significance, confidence intervals or held-out accuracy claims.

limitations: Puga is a published Martian analogue and this is a known-control characterization, not a new analogue discovery.
Filename correspondence links archive specimen IDs; there is no independent chain-of-custody verification here.
Archived mean spectra do not provide replicate observations, calibrated noise covariance or per-band uncertainty. No uncertainty estimate is fabricated from wavelength bins.
A 1 nm export grid is not 1 nm optical resolution. A 20 nm box average supplies common analysis support, but the complete native response and laboratory geometry are unavailable.
Field/lab differences may include specimen preparation, geometry or hydration; these observations alone do not identify the cause.
FTIR CSV amplitude scale is unverified. FTIR remains in native wavenumber/export units and is excluded from reflectance comparison and mineral classification.
XRD data retain native Angle/PSD columns and acquisition headers. No peak-to-mineral labels, phase abundance or independent mineral ground truth are inferred.
Different specimen IDs need not have different mineral assemblages. The mismatch matrix is a descriptive specificity check within a small related archive.

No EMIT/CRISM observation, response function, mask, uncertainty, planetary geological support or orbital mixture is present in this control. Orbital detectability and a new Earth-Mars association remain untested.

uncertainty.reason: Archived means have no replicates or calibrated noise model; wavelength bins and the 90 dependent mismatch pairs are not independent replicates.
